name: Daft Punk
hook: Two Parisians who built French house out of Chicago house and disco samples, then hired Nile Rodgers and recorded Giorgio Moroder telling his life story to make a record without samples.
blurb: Daft Punk were Thomas Bangalter and Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo, from Paris. They started in 1993 after their indie rock band, Darlin', got a bad review that dismissed it as daft, punky thrash, and they took the name from it. Their first album, 'Homework' (1997), was built on the sound of Chicago house. One track, 'Teachers', based on Parris Mitchell's 'Ghetto Shout Out!!' (Dance Mania, 1995), is a list of the house producers and DJs they learned from, including Romanthony, DJ Sneak and Todd Edwards, who they later worked with. 'Discovery' (2001) and the robot helmets they wore in public made them stars. On 'Random Access Memories' (May 2013) they set out, in Bangalter's words as reported by Wikipedia, to do with people what they used to do with machines and samplers. They used session musicians, Nile Rodgers of Chic played guitar on 'Get Lucky', and Giorgio Moroder was recorded telling his life story for 'Giorgio by Moroder'. It won the Grammy for Album of the Year. Kanye West's 'Stronger' (2007) is built on their 'Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger'. They announced their split in February 2021 with a video called 'Epilogue'.

signatureTracks.title: Da Funk
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: A filtered, squelching acid-house riff: their first big single.

signatureTracks.title: Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: A vocoder chant over a chopped funk sample, and the source of Kanye West's 'Stronger'.

signatureTracks.title: Get Lucky
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Nile Rodgers's guitar and Pharrell Williams's voice: disco made by the people, not the samples.
